key_insight: Bulky ligand substituents suppress intermolecular magnetic interactions in a five-copper metallacrown, revealing competing antiferromagnetic couplings and an intrinsic S = 1/2 ground state.
engineering_relevance: The isolated cluster provides a model platform for relating ligand design and exchange interactions to molecular magnetic behavior.
method: Modify salicylhydroxamate ligands with sterically bulky substituents.
Measure static magnetization and X-band/high-frequency EPR.
Compare exchange couplings and g-factors with broken-symmetry DFT.
evidence_signal: Magnetization yields J₁ = −8.1(2) THz and J₂ = −4.40(12) THz, corroborated by DFT, while EPR resolves anisotropic g-factors and supports a thermally accessible excited quartet.
watch_item: Device integration and magnetic behavior outside the studied molecular environment remain unestablished.
paper_title: Magnetism in a homometallic square-planar Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$$_4$Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$ metallacrown
